mainTopic: מעילה on things that come from consecrated animals: blood, milk, eggs and dung, and how the kind of consecration matters
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier argument with רב's ruling: blood let from a live קדשים animal is forbidden for benefit and carries full מעילה. The גמרא then repeats that ruling (גופא) to examine it. רב המנונא challenges it from milk and eggs of הקדש, which have no מעילה. The answer is that an animal cannot live without its blood, but it can live without milk. רב משרשיא challenges again from manure and dung in the עזרה, which an animal also cannot do without, yet they carry no מעילה. The גמרא answers that dung comes from outside food and is always replaced, while blood is part of the animal's own body. The same ברייתא also supports רבי אלעזר's rule that anything 'holy and not holy' is sold and its money goes to the Temple chamber. A new משנה then teaches that milk and eggs of altar animals carry no מעילה, but those of בדק הבית animals do. רב פפא explains that an altar animal consecrated only for its value (קדושת דמים) is treated like בדק הבית. A further משנה begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב's ruling on blood let from a sacrificial animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its previous point by quoting רב: blood let from a live קדשים animal is forbidden for benefit, and one who uses it is liable for מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב said: if someone lets blood from a sacrificial animal, it is forbidden to benefit from that blood, and one who does is liable for מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the discussion from before this text. It quotes רב to back up its point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the גמרא needed a reason why blood could carry מעילה at all. רב's ruling supplies it: blood let from a living sacrificial animal already has full Torah-level מעילה. So blood has a stage where it is truly holy property.

keyTerms.meaning: one who lets blood (bloodletting) from an animal
an animal consecrated as a קרבן
forbidden to get any benefit from
one is liable for מעילה, the misuse of holy property

phrases.english: As Rav said:
One who lets blood from a sacrificial animal,
it is forbidden to benefit from it, and one is liable for misusing it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion by citing רב as support.
steps.raayaObject: That blood can carry מעילה because it has a stage of Torah-level holiness
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling about bloodletting from a קדשים animal

steps.title: Restating רב's ruling to examine it directly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says 'גופא' and repeats רב's ruling, as reported by רב הונא, so it can now analyze the ruling itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the ruling itself. רב הונא said in the name of רב: if someone lets blood from a sacrificial animal, it is forbidden to benefit from it, and one is liable for מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to study רב's ruling on its own terms. This step sets up the challenges that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, רב's ruling was only a tool in another argument. Now the ruling itself is the topic. The repetition here is on purpose: the גמרא is opening a new discussion about it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the matter itself': the גמרא returns to examine a statement it quoted earlier

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an accidental repeat of step 1. 'גופא' tells you the גמרא is quoting the ruling again in order to analyze it.

phrases.english: The matter itself.
Rav Huna said that Rav said:
One who lets blood from a sacrificial animal,
it is forbidden to benefit from it, and one is liable for misusing it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the ruling quoted in step 1 and makes it the new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood let from a live קדשים animal is forbidden for benefit and carries מעילה.

steps.title: Challenge from milk and eggs of consecrated animals
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא objects: milk of consecrated animals and eggs of consecrated doves are forbidden for benefit but carry no מעילה. So why should blood be different?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא objected: the milk of consecrated animals and the eggs of consecrated doves are forbidden for benefit, yet there is no מעילה for them!
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא challenges רב from a teaching about milk and eggs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Milk and eggs come from a consecrated animal, just like blood does. Yet the teaching says they have no מעילה. That suggests things produced by a holy animal do not share its full holiness, which seems to clash with רב's ruling about blood.

keyTerms.meaning: the milk of consecrated animals
eggs of turtledoves (consecrated birds)
forbidden for benefit, but no liability for מעילה

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna raised an objection:
The milk of consecrated animals and the eggs of doves,
one may not benefit from them, but there is no liability for misuse!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling restated in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that blood from a קדשים animal carries מעילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Milk and eggs are also products of a consecrated animal, yet they carry no מעילה. So blood should not carry it either.

steps.title: Blood is different because an animal cannot live without it
steps.stepSummary: The answer: רב's rule applies only to blood, since an animal cannot survive without its blood. Milk is different, because an animal can live without it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered him: when we said this, we meant blood, because the animal cannot live without blood. But milk, which the animal can live without, does not carry מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered by showing that blood and milk are not the same kind of thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood is needed for the animal's life, so it counts as part of the animal itself. That is why it carries the animal's מעילה. Milk is not needed for the animal to live, so it is just something that comes from the animal, and it has no מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: is able to exist or survive
regarding, in the case of

steps.whatToRemember: The test for whether a product of a holy animal carries מעילה: can the animal live without it? Blood: no, so there is מעילה. Milk: yes, so there is no מעילה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כִּי קָאָמְרִינַן, לְגַבֵּי דָּם,
phrases.english: He said to him: when we said this, it was regarding blood,
since the animal cannot survive without blood.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל חֵלֶב, דְּקָא מִקַּיְימָא בְּלֹא חֵלֶב – לָא.
phrases.english: But milk, since the animal survives without milk, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כִּי קָאָמְרִינַן, לְגַבֵּי דָּם
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every product of a consecrated animal should be treated the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only something the animal cannot live without, like blood, counts as the animal itself and carries מעילה.

steps.title: Challenge from manure and dung in the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא objects: manure and dung in the עזרה carry no מעילה, and the money from selling them goes to the Temple chamber.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא objected: the manure and dung in the courtyard may not be used for benefit, but there is no מעילה for them, and the money from selling them goes to the Temple chamber.
steps.whatsHappening: A second challenge is raised, this time from manure and dung. Step 6 spells out the challenge, and step 7 answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge tests the new rule from step 4, that what an animal cannot live without counts as the animal. The point seems to be that an animal also cannot live without producing waste, yet manure and dung carry no מעילה. Notice that the money from selling them still goes to הקדש, so they keep some holiness, just not מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: manure (dried waste)
dung (waste still in or just out of the animal's body)
the Temple treasury chamber
its money (sale price) shall go to

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya raised an objection:
The manure and the dung that are in the courtyard,
phrases.notes: The courtyard here is the Temple courtyard, the עזרה.

phrases.english: one may not benefit from them, and there is no liability for misuse.
And their money goes to the chamber.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction just made in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that whatever an animal cannot live without counts as the animal and carries מעילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An animal also cannot live without producing waste, yet manure and dung carry no מעילה.

steps.title: Dung is also something the animal cannot live without
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא's challenge is spelled out: by the logic of the last answer, dung should carry מעילה just like blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is there no מעילה on dung? Here too, an animal cannot survive without dung!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the challenge from the previous step. If blood carries מעילה because the animal cannot live without it, dung should too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said blood is different from milk because an animal cannot survive without blood. But an animal also cannot survive without producing dung. Yet the ברייתא says dung in the עזרה carries no מעילה, so the reason given in step 4 seems too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
Here too; the same logic applies here
Cannot survive

phrases.english: Why? Here too,
phrases.notes: He means: why does the ברייתא say there is no מעילה on dung?

phrases.english: it cannot survive without dung!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? הָכָא נָמֵי, לָא מְקַיֵּים בְּלֹא פֶּרֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge that step 5 began by citing the ברייתא about dung.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 4: blood carries מעילה because an animal cannot survive without it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Dung also fits the description 'the animal cannot survive without it,' yet it carries no מעילה. So that description cannot be the real reason.

steps.title: Dung comes from outside, blood is part of the body
steps.stepSummary: Dung is not comparable, because it comes from outside food and is constantly replaced. Blood is part of the animal's own body.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: How can you compare? This dung comes to the animal from outside. This dung leaves and other dung comes. That excludes blood, which comes from the animal's own body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Dung is just passing food that keeps getting replaced, while blood belongs to the animal's body itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer makes step 4's reason more precise. It is not enough that the animal 'needs' something. It must also be a real part of the animal's own body, as blood is. Dung comes from food eaten from the outside world and is always being replaced, so it is not part of the consecrated animal.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? Why bring up this case?
From the outside world
To exclude
From its own body

steps.whatToRemember: Blood carries מעילה because it is part of the animal's own body and the animal cannot live without it. Milk can be done without, and dung comes from outside food and keeps being replaced, so neither carries מעילה.

phrases.english: They say: How can you compare?
This dung
comes to it from the outside world,
phrases.notes: He means it comes from the food the animal ate.

phrases.english: this one goes out, and another one comes.
That excludes blood, which comes from its own body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dung challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: refines the reason by adding that the thing must be part of the animal's own body.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anything the animal cannot live without, including dung, should carry מעילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only something that is part of the animal's own body and that it cannot live without, like blood, carries מעילה. Dung comes from outside and keeps being replaced.

steps.title: The ברייתא supports רבי אלעזר about money going to the chamber
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא about dung says 'no benefit, no מעילה, and its money goes to the chamber.' This supports רבי אלעזר's general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא teaches: one may not benefit from it, there is no מעילה, and its money goes to the chamber. This supports רבי אלעזר, who said: Wherever the Sages said something is holy and not holy, its money goes to the Temple chamber.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes that the ברייתא about dung backs up a general rule taught by רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dung is in an in-between status. You may not benefit from it, but there is no מעילה. רבי אלעזר taught that anything in this 'holy and not holy' status is sold, and the money goes to the Temple chamber. The ברייתא says exactly this about dung, so it supports him.

keyTerms.meaning: This supports him
Its money; what it is sold for
Holy and not holy: a halfway status of הקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word דָּמָיו means 'its money,' not 'its blood,' even though the sugya has been talking about blood (דם).

phrases.english: It teaches:
phrases.notes: This refers to the ברייתא about manure and dung in the עזרה from step 5.

phrases.english: one may not benefit, but there is no liability for misuse,
and its money goes to the chamber.
This supports רבי אלעזר,
as רבי אלעזר said:
Wherever the Sages said
something is holy and not holy,
its money goes to the chamber.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָתָנֵי לֹא נֶהֱנִין וְלֹא מוֹעֲלִין וְדָמָיו לַלִּשְׁכָּה. מְסַיְּיעָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the blood and dung question and draws a side lesson from the same ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's rule: anything 'holy and not holy' is sold, and its money goes to the Temple chamber.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about manure and dung in the עזרה: no benefit, no מעילה, and its money goes to the chamber.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a general rule for every in-between הקדש item. Even without מעילה, its value still belongs to the Temple.

steps.title: משנה: milk of consecrated animals and eggs of doves
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: one may not benefit from milk of consecrated animals or eggs of consecrated doves, but there is no מעילה on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The milk of consecrated animals and the eggs of consecrated turtledoves: one may not benefit from them, but there is no מעילה on them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules that milk and eggs of consecrated animals have the 'forbidden but no מעילה' status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the source רב המנונא quoted in step 3 to challenge רב. Milk and eggs are forbidden for benefit, but there is no מעילה on them. The next step limits this rule to animals consecrated for the altar.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Milk of consecrated animals
Turtledoves, a kind of bird used for offerings
One may not benefit

phrases.english: MISHNAH: The milk of consecrated animals
and the eggs of consecrated turtledoves:
one may not benefit from them, but there is no מעילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Milk of consecrated animals and eggs of consecrated doves are forbidden for benefit, but there is no מעילה.

steps.title: Only altar offerings, not animals given for Temple upkeep
steps.stepSummary: The משנה limits its rule to animals consecrated for the altar. With animals consecrated for בדק הבית, there is מעילה on the milk and eggs too.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? With animals consecrated for the altar. But with things consecrated for Temple upkeep, if someone consecrated a hen, there is מעילה on it and its egg. If he consecrated a donkey, there is מעילה on it and its milk.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה narrows its own rule. 'No מעילה on milk and eggs' applies only to altar offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An altar offering's holiness is about the animal being brought on the altar. Its milk and eggs are not brought, so they stay apart from it. When something is given to בדק הבית for its value, the whole thing is consecrated, so its eggs and milk are consecrated with it and carry מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: When is this said? This limits the rule just stated
Things consecrated to be offered on the altar
Things consecrated for the Temple's upkeep and repairs
A hen
A female donkey

steps.whatToRemember: Milk and eggs of altar offerings: forbidden, but no מעילה. Milk and eggs of animals given to בדק הבית: full מעילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the kind of holiness matters: being holy for the altar works differently from being holy for its value to the Temple.

phrases.english: When is this said?
With animals consecrated for the altar.
But with things consecrated for Temple upkeep,
if he consecrated a hen,
there is מעילה on it and on its egg;
if he consecrated a donkey,
there is מעילה on it and on its milk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule from step 9 to altar offerings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'no מעילה' rule for milk and eggs applies only to altar offerings. When an animal is consecrated for בדק הבית, there is מעילה on the animal and on its eggs or milk.

steps.title: What about an altar animal consecrated only for its value?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: does even an animal consecrated for the altar only for its money value have no מעילה on its milk and eggs?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: But for the altar, if he consecrated it with only a sanctity of its value, is there really no מעילה on it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule from Step 9. If someone consecrated an animal for the altar only so its value could be used, should its milk and eggs really be free of מעילה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said the 'no מעילה' rule is only for altar animals, while בדק הבית animals do have מעילה on their milk and eggs. But an animal dedicated only for its money value is really just like a בדק הבית item, since the animal itself won't be offered. So why should it be treated more leniently?

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Holiness of value: the item is holy only for its money, to be sold and the money used
For the altar, meaning set aside for offerings
The sin of misusing something holy, which requires paying back plus a fifth and a קרבן

phrases.english: Gemara:
But regarding the altar,
when he consecrated it with a sanctity of value,
phrases.notes: He means the animal will be sold and the money used for an offering. The animal itself won't go on the altar.

phrases.english: is there no מעילה on it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא גַּבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ, כִּי אַקְדְּשַׁהּ קְדוּשַּׁת דָּמִים, לָא אִית בַּהּ מְעִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the line drawn in Step 10 between altar animals and בדק הבית animals.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's blanket rule that milk and eggs of altar-consecrated animals carry no מעילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An animal consecrated only for its value is really like a בדק הבית item, so it should get בדק הבית's stricter rule of מעילה on milk and eggs.

steps.title: רב פפא fills in missing words in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the משנה is missing a line. The leniency is only for animals with קדושת הגוף. An animal with קדושת דמים is like בדק הבית, so a consecrated hen or donkey carries מעילה on its eggs or milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it teaches. When is this said? When he consecrated the animal's body itself for the altar. But if he consecrated it only for its value for the altar, it is as if he consecrated it for בדק הבית. So if he consecrated a hen, there is מעילה on it and its egg. If he consecrated a donkey, there is מעילה on it and its milk.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא agrees with the challenge. He explains that the משנה left out a line that limits its rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'no מעילה on milk and eggs' rule covers only an animal whose own body is holy for the altar (קדושת הגוף). An animal dedicated only for its value is treated exactly like a בדק הבית item, so its milk and eggs are fully subject to מעילה. The hen and donkey are the examples of this case.

keyTerms.meaning: The text is missing words, and the גמרא fills them in
Holiness of the body: the item itself is holy and meant to be offered
It is treated as if he had consecrated it (for a different purpose)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two kinds of altar consecration. With קדושת הגוף, there is no מעילה on milk or eggs. With קדושת דמים, the animal is treated like בדק הבית, so there is מעילה on milk and eggs.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the hen or donkey stops being consecrated 'for the altar.' It still is. It simply gets the בדק הבית outcome for מעילה, because only its value is holy.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the type of holiness, not just where the item is headed, decides whether its products carry מעילה.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
It is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
In what case are these words said?
When he consecrated it with bodily sanctity for the altar,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הִקְדִּישׁוֹ קְדוּשַּׁת דָּמִים לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ –
phrases.english: but if he consecrated it with a sanctity of value for the altar,
it becomes as if he consecrated it for Temple upkeep.
If he consecrated a hen, there is מעילה on it and on its egg,
a donkey: there is מעילה on it and on its milk.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: חַסּוֹרֵי מִיחַסְּרָא וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 11 by reading missing words into the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual completion (חסורי מחסרא): the משנה is read with an added limiting clause.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say that every altar consecration, even קדושת דמים, frees milk and eggs from מעילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only קדושת הגוף for the altar frees milk and eggs from מעילה. קדושת דמים is like בדק הבית, so there is מעילה on the animal and its products.

steps.title: A new משנה begins: anything fit for the altar
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens with the words 'anything that is fit for the altar.'
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Anything that is fit for the altar...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא's discussion is over, and a new משנה begins. Only its opening words appear here. It is setting up a new rule about items fit for the altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This starts a new topic. The rest of the rule continues past this point, so for now we only know its subject: consecrated items that are fit to be offered on the altar.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, the base text the גמרא discusses
Fit for the altar, meaning valid to be offered

phrases.english: Mishnah: Anything that is fit for the altar

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The opening of a rule about consecrated items fit for the altar. The ruling itself continues on the next amud.
